items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: Louis Moreau Gottschalk was in fact French.

ctx.x: I know. Is it Al Hirt? Is it the Neville Brothers? Is it Mannie Fresh? Is it Pete Fountain? What is it? It’s like it’s not a style it’s an attitude of playing music under water. Because in New Orleans we’re under water. Danny Barker used to say that. That’s why trumpet players from there, that’s why Nicholas Payton, Al Hirt, that’s why these trumpet players have such a big sound. It’s like you know you go to a baseball game and a batter puts weights on his bats and swings it? They have to push against this weight…

to get the sound waves to push the water out of the way so we can hear it. I know that sounds a little metaphysical. But the point is creating and performing music below sea level is a different physical process than gasping for air in Denver or playing bebop in New York. So that’s part of why people from New Orleans sound different. I mean what sets New Orleans pianists apart? I mean Allen Toussaint sounded very French, very ornate, very French. Louis Moreau Gottschalk was in fact French. James Booker did a lot…
